nodes.label: Rebalance
nodes.rationale: Three triggers: membership change, the periodic strategy poll, and a region deregistering as it stops. Rebalance is work-shedding, not work-seeking — an idle node gets newly allocated shards but never has existing ones moved into it just for being quiet.

nodes.label: HandOff
nodes.rationale: Marks the shard handing-off: the region keeps receiving messages for its entities but buffers them instead of forwarding, so nothing races past a half-moved entity.

nodes.label: HandOffComplete
nodes.rationale: Sent once every entity in the shard is gone; only then does the coordinator run allocate() for a new home.

nodes.label: Buffered messages during handoff
nodes.rationale: A message sent during handoff is delayed, not lost — the cost is latency spikes in rebalance windows, and the buffer is unbounded so memory needs watching under load. Re-asking the coordinator matters more than it looks: a completed handoff clears the old region's cached shard home, and the coordinator announces a new placement only to the new owner and regions with an open request, so without the re-ask a shard that goes quiet after rebalance would leave the buffer sitting forever.

nodes.label: Region deregistration on stop
nodes.rationale: Covers a region stopped on a node that stays in the cluster, where no membership event fires at all. Without it a stopped region orphaned its shards: the coordinator still named it as their home, senders cached that home and delivered into a stopped actor, and nothing recovered because the candidate set is derived from the registry with no liveness check. Best-effort and idempotent.

nodes.label: Coordinator-only directive authorization
nodes.rationale: HandOff, ShardHome, RememberedEntities, ShardMapUpdate and RegisterAcknowledgment are checked on where they came from, never on a payload field the sender writes: the frame must arrive stamped with the peer the connection authenticated as, and that peer must be the node the region currently believes hosts the coordinator. Until this rule existed any peer that completed the handshake could wipe a shard's entities with a small frame, arbitrarily often. Dropping is safe by construction because a region re-registers and re-asks on the next leader or membership event. This is authorization, not authentication — run mTLS if the network is not trusted.

nodes.label: Forced reallocation on handoff timeout
nodes.rationale: When HandOffComplete misses handOffTimeoutMs the coordinator warns and reallocates anyway, so the old entities may still be alive on the source node and receiving local messages — split-brain entities until the orphans die. Causes: a hanging postStop or a partition mid-handoff.

nodes.label: handOffTimeoutMs
nodes.rationale: Tune to worst-case persist time plus slack; a slow postStop overshoots the 10s default and triggers forced reallocation with orphan-entity risk.
